correctness.rationale: For f(x)=Lx²/2 the exact Bregman curvature difference is (L/2)(x_k−x_{k−1})², reducing Algorithm 2 test to λ_{k−1}>τ=2η0/L and its reset output to r=2η1/L; otherwise λ grows by 1+ε_{k−1}. After consecutive resets disjoint expansion-factor blocks each exceed τ/r=η0/η1, so total finite P yields N−1<log P/log(η0/η1) and N≤ceil(log P/log ratio), including N=1 when P=1. Since all later positive factors would trigger a new reset above τ, the post-last-reset stepsizes increase to λ∞∈(r,τ]. An explicit positive summable dyadic product realizes each λ∞, and scalar gradient recurrence gives asymptotic |1−Lλ∞|. For η0≤1/2 this gives [1−2η0,1−2η1); small λ0 with no reset yields factor near one. Finite-termination and never-reset branches are scoped separately; numerical verifier is supporting only.
residual_risks: The reset count uses an expansion product P over the full prescribed infinite sequence, not only factors before the first reset; this can overestimate actual resets and is still valid.
